comments.author: jacquesm
comments.story: Mercedes-Benz conducting the biggest test using drones to ship everyday items
comments.text: You should definitely watch this: [LINK] and [VIDEO] Also, while birds are really good at using their wings to glide and provide propulsion flapping designs that need to lift much more than their own weight have so far not worked very well. So I don't really see them as viable for packages.

comments.author: Animats
comments.story: The first autonomous, entirely soft robot
comments.why: Festo's Smart Bird shows advanced bio-inspired robotics
comments.text: This is "autonomous" at the windup toy level. Festo, the German robotics company, is way ahead in autonomous soft robots. See their "Air Ray" fly around[1] Each year, Festo makes motion controllers and robots, especially high-precision pneumatic devices. Each year, they build something awesome. They do have some rigid components, but if they wanted to build one with fluidic logic, they certainly could. Their Smart Bird is spectacular.[2] Festo is a big, family-owned engineering company. 18,700 employees. founded in 1925. Annual sales €2.64 billion. One of the most innovative companies in mechanical engineering, yet a totally different business model than Silicon Valley's. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
